design_intent: Reduce high-angle summer solar gain at the valley-facing glass gable while retaining daylight, the full ground-floor glass wall and an unobstructed seated valley view.

shared_constraints.ground_floor_glazing: continuous full-width glass from finished floor to the 3.0 m transom
shared_constraints.valley_view: no fixed shading element may cross the ground-floor vision zone
shared_constraints.materials: matte-black metal coordinated with the window surround and black Belgian roof
shared_constraints.site: retain the hedge, neighbouring brick building, narrow paved passage, lawn and valley outlook

options.name: Deep roof visor
options.summary: A 1.60 m extension of both roof planes at the valley gable. The glass remains completely open below and the architecture stays closest to a traditional Belgian barn.

options.name: Floating brise-soleil
options.summary: A 1.00 m roof extension plus an open 1.25 m-deep horizontal blade canopy aligned just above the 3.0 m transom. The ground-floor glass and eye-level view remain untouched.
options.solar_priority: strong high-angle control with filtered daylight

options.name: Upper-gable veil
options.summary: A 1.25 m roof extension with spaced operable vertical fins over only the triangular upper glass. The complete rectangular ground-floor glass wall remains unobstructed.
options.solar_priority: adjustable glare and low-angle control at the upper gable
